trust_decision.summary: {fetch} may open a remote resource only if the security policy's trusted_uri regex matches scheme://host of the *initial* URL (isTrustedUri in handle()); the URL then goes to file_get_contents() for every non-'http' scheme, which follows redirects, so the trust decision is never applied to the final destination.

landing_point.why: The summary names {fetch} and a redirect bypass, so an engineer reads the {fetch} handler: the isTrustedUri gate at :36-48 and the file_get_contents() call that follows redirects at :192.

fix_sites.entry_point: {fetch} template function tag (compiled handler used by Smarty::fetch()/display())

fix_sites.where: fix.diff:164-193 (libs/plugins/function.fetch.php, v4 branch port; file not present at the pinned commit)
fix_sites.module_kind: legacy plugin function (second implementation, other major branch)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: {html_image} is a different tag from the {fetch} named in the advisory, its remote path already has its own isTrustedUri() branch and uses getimagesize(), which takes no stream context, so a solver can call redirect handling there a separate feature/rewrite rather than part of this bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Without a security policy, remote {fetch} of a redirecting URL must keep following redirects (PHP default), and http:// URLs must keep using the manual fsockopen branch (which also populates assign_headers); an over-broad fix that disables redirects unconditionally or routes every scheme through file_get_contents breaks both.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/FunctionHandler/Fetch.php:192 and src/FunctionHandler/Fetch.php:50-190; expected behaviour asserted by fix.diff:77-89

O6_input_shapes: https:// (only the exact scheme 'http' takes the fsockopen branch at src/FunctionHandler/Fetch.php:50, so every other scheme reaches file_get_contents at :192)
other 'scheme://' forms: ftp://, and custom/PHP stream wrappers (e.g. a registered ssrftest:// wrapper)
uppercase scheme (lowercased for detection at src/FunctionHandler/Fetch.php:32-35)
file:// prefixed path (stripped at src/FunctionHandler/Fetch.php:29-31, then treated as local)
local path with no scheme (local branch, isTrustedResourceDir)
no security policy at all (redirects remain enabled, backwards compatible)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: {html_image file="https://trusted/..."} without width/height passes isTrustedUri() and then fetches through getimagesize(), which uses PHP's default http context and follows redirects to a non-trusted host
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different tag from the {fetch} in the advisory; getimagesize() accepts no stream context, so making it redirect-safe means fetching with file_get_contents() + getimagesizefromstring(), i.e. a rewrite of a neighbouring feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (Smarty\FunctionHandler) but a different file from the landing point; reachable from any template

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Remote template source resolved through the stream resource path (e.g. {include file="https://host/tpl"}): fopen() at :59 is called with no context, so redirects are followed, and the only check is isTrustedStream() on the scheme
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Remote streams are governed by the separate $streams allow-list, which defaults to ['file'], so this route throws unless a deployment explicitly opts in to the https stream; it never was a trusted_uri route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package away (Smarty\Resource vs Smarty\FunctionHandler), and reached from the resource loader rather than a tag handler

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a redirect-safe stream fetch (add a no-redirect stream context to the fopen() call, or an isTrustedUri check on the resource name)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Smarty already lets templates load sources via PHP stream wrappers and this class is the only place that opens them; a maintainer hardening remote fetches would plausibly patch it while still missing redirects because the gate here is isTrustedStream, not trusted_uri.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a legacy smarty_function_fetch-style implementation delegated through the BC wrapper (the v4 branch still ships libs/plugins/function.fetch.php)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: v5 keeps a compatibility wrapper for old-style plugin callbacks and addPluginsDir() still loads user plugin directories, so an old fetch implementation calling @file_get_contents() can sit next to the new handler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deprecated stream-variable reader that fopen()s a 'scheme://name' string with no security check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The parser still emits getStreamVariable() for {$x:y} syntax and the code predates the security policy, so a maintainer could add a trusted_uri/stream check here without touching redirects.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918): server-side request forgery via HTTP redirects bypassing a trusted_uri allow-list
